title: Anas ibn Malik
hook: served the Prophet ten years and never once heard him ask, why did you do that

segments.voice: Yesterday: Abu Hurayrah, named for the little cat, who made listening his work. Your line was father of the kitten.

A boy is sent on an errand. He says out loud that he won't go, though inside he means to. On the way through the market he comes upon some children playing, and there he stops. The errand waits. Then a hand takes him gently by the back of the neck. He looks up, and the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, is laughing. Little Anas, did you go where I asked you? Yes, says the boy, I'm going now. Sahih Muslim keeps the scene, told by the boy himself. Today: the servant who was never scolded.
screen: `AN ERRAND, AND A GAME.` → `A HAND ON THE NECK.` → `HE WAS LAUGHING.`

segments.voice: Anas ibn Malik came into the Prophet's household as a boy. Bukhari records his mother, Umm Sulaym, saying to the Prophet: Anas is your servant; pray for him. And the Prophet did. Years later Anas summed up that house in one sentence that both Bukhari and Muslim keep. I served the Prophet for ten years, and he never said to me so much as uff. Never, about something I had done, why did you do that? Never, about something I had left undone, why didn't you do that? Ten years of jobs in a busy household. Some done badly, some forgotten, some put off while a boy stopped among children at play. Anas doesn't say he was perfect. He says he was never made to answer for it with a sharp word. And notice the word he picks: uff. Not a lecture or a punishment, just the smallest sigh of annoyance, the noise people make before they even think. The Qur'an uses that same little word in the surah called the Night Journey, telling believers not to say uff to aging parents. Anas reports he never heard even that much. Some teachers cite this hadith on the Prophet's character, and on how to treat anyone who works for you or under you: children, students, staff. Ten years of small failures, met with patience.
screen: `YOUR SERVANT. PRAY FOR HIM.` · `TEN YEARS IN THE HOUSE.` · `NOT EVEN UFF.` · `NEVER: WHY DID YOU DO THAT?` · then, large: `TEN YEARS, NO SCOLDING.`

segments.voice: Think of the person you're most likely to snap at, and the small thing they might get wrong: the late reply, the dish left out, the job half done. Picture that moment, and let the uff go out with your breath before it reaches your mouth; then choose what you'd say instead, a question, a joke, or nothing at all. If you pray, you can ask for patience with that one person.
Uff, the smallest sigh of annoyance, the word Anas ibn Malik said he never heard in ten years serving the Prophet's house. Today's word.
Your line: ten years, no scolding. Not even the smallest sigh. Day eight hundred thirty-eight, done.

howItsDone: Muslims often cite Anas's report of ten years without a harsh word when teaching about the Prophet's character and about kindness to children, students and anyone who works for them.

take him by the neck, laughing, and ask if he went.

fork.reveal: Anas says he looked up and the Prophet was laughing: did you go where I asked? yes, I'm going.

original.note: Arabic: the smallest sound of annoyance, the word Anas says he never heard.

trapdoor: what you thought: a servant boy who did everything right.
what it means: a boy who forgot things and dawdled, and was never met with even a sigh of blame.
what a scholar hears: uff, the same tiny word the Qur'an tells believers not to say to aging parents (17:23).
recall: the Persian seeker who found the Prophet

chat.says: What did Anas mean when he said the Prophet never even said uff to him?
options: In ten years serving him, Anas never got even a sigh of annoyance.
Anas never made a mistake, so there was nothing to be annoyed about.
The Prophet only corrected Anas in private, never in front of others.
chat.meaning: Anas served ten years and never heard uff, or why did you do that. He doesn't claim he was perfect; he was never scolded.

Anas ibn Malik.meaning: a companion who served in the Prophet's house as a boy

Umm Sulaym.meaning: Anas's mother, who asked the Prophet to pray for him

uff.meaning: a small sound of annoyance, like a sigh

Sahih Muslim.meaning: a major collection of the Prophet's sayings

sources.ref: Sahih Muslim 2309 / Sahih al-Bukhari 6038 (ten years, never uff, never why did you do that)

notes: Hadith numbers cited from memory (Muslim 2309, 2310; Bukhari 6038, 6334); confirm.
Muslim 2310 uses the diminutive 'Unays'; rendered as 'little Anas'. Confirm.
Myth item: some versions of 6038 mention the period as nine or ten years; the cited Muslim/Bukhari wording says ten. Confirm.
'Teachers cite this hadith when they talk about...' is a general description of how the hadith is used; confirm.
